title: Compact export + allocator: micro-consumption ledger UX for token-level attribution
creator: Jaspreet Kaur
description:
Background: Product teams need a lightweight, exportable ledger that surfaces per-message and per-token cost attribution for mixed workloads (chat, batch generation, embeddings). Existing cost views are high-fidelity dashboards but too heavy for quick audits and downstream chargeback flows. Goal: design a compact ledger view and CSV/JSON export format that makes allocation, attribution, and pricing assumptions explicit, while supporting role-aware exports and sampling to limit data size.

Scope: deliver a compact table UI for Console -> Cost -> Microledger; an export button with configurable column presets and privacy-safe sampling; a small inline allocator panel that shows cost splits (prompt/system/function/completion + model/quantization tier). Work includes prototype screens, copy for pricing-preview, export schema, and usability test notes.

Users: finance engineer reconciling billing, platform engineer validating rollout impact, customer success doing diagnostics, and internal billing integrations that consume CSVs.

Non-goals: not building the backend export pipeline here (engineering will define storage/retention). Not replacing the detailed per-route cost dashboards — this is complementary compact export UX.
acceptance_criteria: Compact ledger UI shows collapsible rows with message-level granularity and per-token cost columns (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, system_tokens, function_tokens)
Export flow allows selecting preset columns (compact, full, audit) and exports CSV/JSON with documented schema and pricing assumptions header
Inline allocator panel displays percentage splits and monetary amounts and exposes a small 'apply SKU' dropdown for previewing alternate pricing scenarios
Exports respect RBAC: users without export permission see a masked preview and a request flow
Sampling option available: sample rate control (e.g., 1/1, 1/10, 1/100) with deterministic sampling seed for reproducibility
Prototype tested with 6 participants showing average task success >= 85% for exporting an audit CSV and interpreting attribution columns
design_links: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/compact-microledger-v1 (figma: compact ledger, allocator panel, export modal)
comments: 2025-02-14 Jaspreet Kaur: Kickoff - scoped compact ledger with engineering & PM. Agreed baseline columns and three export presets (compact, audit, full).
2025-02-17 Maya Li: First prototype uploaded. Focused on horizontal density, small type, and inline allocator that opens as a popover. Asked for microcopy edits on SKU preview.

2025-02-18 Arjun Patel (ENG): Feasibility note - backend can supply per-token breakdown but full exports for large time ranges need sampling. We'll expose deterministic sampling and chunked export endpoints. Will add API contract link.

2025-02-19 Emma Ruiz (PM): Suggested adding 'pricing-preview' mode that applies hypothetical rate cards so customers can preview cost impact of switching quantization/model tiers. High priority for Sales demos.

2025-02-20 Usability session summary: 6 participants (2 finance, 2 platform, 2 CS). Confusion on 'system token' label; changed to 'system / metadata tokens'. Export presets were well understood; one user asked for an 'anonymize' toggle for user IDs.
2025-02-21 Design review notes: Reduce row chrome, add two-line column descriptions in export modal, and expose sample size estimate when sampling is enabled.
decisions: Use three export presets: compact (minimal columns), audit (adds trace/context IDs and message text hashes), full (every available telemetry field)
Include a small header block in CSV/JSON export containing export parameters (time range, sample rate, pricing-preview applied, SKU used, generated_at) to make downstream reconciliation deterministic
Show pricing-preview dropdown inside allocator panel that applies selected SKU locally in the browser without requiring server-side recalculation for quick feedback
Default sampling to 1/10 for ranges > 7 days with an option to request full export (requires engineering approval)
next_steps: Finalize copy for column descriptions and anonymization guidance (Jaspreet)
Handoff Figma frames and proposed CSS tokens to engineering (Maya)
Add API contract for export endpoint and deterministic sampling to ENG ticket (Arjun) - reference in PRD
Run one round of follow-up usability testing after microcopy changes (schedule Week of 2025-03-03)
Prepare demo flow for sales using pricing-preview with two SKU scenarios (standard / enterprise)
